identity: Biochemist and university teacher · United States · 1918–1999
title: Gertrude B. Elion's birth chart
metaDescription: Gertrude B. Elion's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.9° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Mars sit 0.6° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads identity and drive as a single working part. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aquarius, but precisely: 2.9°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (8.4°), Venus in Aquarius (28.3°), Mars in Libra (2.3°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts the Sun a third of the circle apart from Mars, 0.6° off exact. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, Mars trine Jupiter at 0.8°, and the Sun trine Jupiter at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: the Sun, Mars, Jupiter close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it. Mercury opposes Pluto while both square Mars. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aquarius at 2.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Libra at 2.3° is in detriment; Jupiter in Gemini at 1.5° is in detriment; Saturn in Leo at 11.8° is in detriment. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 6 air, 2 fire, 1 earth, 1 water; by modality, 5 fixed, 3 cardinal, 2 mutable. Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.8° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 23.4°.
